s1.syndrome_frame: A cardiac abnormality with a systolic murmur and abnormal ECG findings in a young pregnant woman
salient_findings: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
No history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
Vital parameters within normal limits
Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
No significant ST-T segment changes on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
Normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
Pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium are consistent with an atrial septal defect.

rejected.label: Ventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: The echocardiogram shows a defect with a left-to-right shunt, but the location is not specified as ventricular.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: There is no mention of atrioventricular valve abnormalities or other characteristic features of this defect.

rejected.label: Patent Foramen Ovale
rejected.why: The size of the defect (21 mm) is larger than what is typically seen with a patent foramen ovale.

rejected.label: Ebstein's Anomaly
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic features such as apical displacement of the tricuspid valve or right ventricular dysfunction.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Regurgitation
rejected.why: While tricuspid regurgitation can be associated with atrial septal defects, it is not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection
rejected.why: There is no mention of abnormal pulmonary venous connections.

rejected.label: Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection
rejected.why: There is no mention of abnormal pulmonary venous connections, and the step-up in oxygenation is consistent with an atrial septal defect.
